challenge.method: Tested whether the shared licence name and 2007 copyright line could conceal a duplicate of 1.0. Compared the opening notices and section 5 copyleft clauses, checked the 1.2 annex for possible substitution, and matched the 1.1 editorial row to the prospective entity.
challenge.results: The 1.1 notice specifies its edition. Its section 5 copyleft clause expressly addresses later versions and an original work restricted to this version. The corresponding 1.0 clause specifies this licence. The 2017 annex bears a 1.2 title. Neither alternative matches the 1.1 rendering, and the matching editorial row makes active status conditional on qualification.

limitations: The web observation covers the visible English representation. Original PDF byte identity, adoption dates, equivalence across languages, redistribution, installation and grants for a particular work are outside this finding.
The statement carries the qualification condition. The empty conditions array and the value active, read alone, do not establish that admission and review gates have passed.
reasoning: The English document at the Interoperable Europe URL identifies itself as EUPL v.1.1 in both its title and its opening notice. The Index decision assigns the corresponding prospective entity the display name European Union Public Licence v. 1.1, kind license and state active upon qualification.
